mainTopic: A delayed גט left at the sides of the public street; a husband's right to make his wife swear about managing his property, and releasing her from that oath.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion: a court may force someone to keep a positive מצוה, such as paying a debt. Then רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא about a גט that takes effect only after thirty days, which the woman left at צידי רשות הרבים (the sides of the public street). In one version רב חסדא says she is not divorced, learning from רב ושמואל that things lying in public are not acquired. רמי בר חמא counters with רב נחמן's case of a cow acquired after thirty days while standing in an אגם (open meadow). In a second version the two sides are swapped, and each comparison is rejected because these places are each their own category. A new משנה follows: a husband who makes his wife a storekeeper or a manager of his property may make her swear whenever he wants, and רבי אליעזר says this covers even her spinning and her dough. The גמרא proves from a ברייתא that רבי אליעזר allows that oath from the start, not only by adding it onto another oath (גלגול). The next משנה teaches how a husband can write in the כתובה that he gives up his right to make her swear, and how far that release reaches: to her heirs, to his heirs, and to a widow who managed the estate. The amud ends as the גמרא asks what oath the husband had over her in the first place, and רב's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the previous discussion: the court may force a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the earlier discussion: the court may strike a person until he agrees to do a positive מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court strikes him, even until his soul departs.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the previous discussion. It ends by saying a court can use force on someone who refuses to do a positive מצוה, like paying back a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying a debt counts as a positive מצוה. When a person refuses to do a positive מצוה‎, בית דין does not just give him a set punishment. It may keep pressuring him with no limit until he agrees to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the court) strike him
Until his soul departs. Pressure with no fixed limit.

steps.whatToRemember: A court can force a person to do a positive מצוה, including paying his debts.

phrases.english: They strike him
until his soul departs.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַכִּין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The court may force someone without limit until he does a positive מצוה, such as repaying a debt.

steps.title: A delayed divorce document left at the sides of the public street
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks: if a גט takes effect only after thirty days and the woman put it at צידי רשות הרבים, is she divorced?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: A man told his wife, "Here is your גט, but you are divorced with it only after thirty days." She went and put it at the sides of the public street. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא about a גט that only works after thirty days, which the woman left at the edge of a public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט works only at the end of the thirty days. At that moment it must be in the woman's possession. Here it is lying at צידי רשות הרבים, an area next to the public street, so the question is whether she still holds it in a way that counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question to a teacher or colleague)
Your bill of divorce (גט)
After thirty days
The sides or edges of the public domain
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: She was handed the גט right away. The problem is only where the גט is lying when the thirty days end and the divorce is supposed to take effect.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked of Rav Ḥisda:
"This is your bill of divorce,
but you will not be divorced with it
except after thirty days,"
and she went and placed it
at the sides of the public domain,
phrases.notes: This is the strip along the edge of a public street. It is open to the street but is not the main walkway.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the closing line before it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a delayed גט lying at צידי רשות הרבים when the thirty days end still divorces the woman.

steps.title: רב חסדא: she is not divorced, based on רב ושמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules she is not divorced. רב ושמואל hold that things lying in רשות הרבים are not acquired, and the sides of the public street count as public street.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: She is not divorced. We learn this from רב ושמואל, who both said: "And that is only when the items are piled up and lying in the public domain." And the sides of the public domain are like the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that she is not divorced. He supports this with a statement of רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל explained an earlier משנה. Creditors may grab a dead man's movable items only when those items are lying in רשות הרבים, because there the heirs never acquired them. In the same way, a גט lying in public is not in the woman's possession. רב חסדא then adds that צידי רשות הרבים has the same status as the street itself.

keyTerms.meaning: She is not divorced
Both of them
Piled up and lying there
The public domain
They are considered like

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument depends on one claim: the sides of a public street count as the public street. This is exactly the point רמי בר חמא will challenge next.

phrases.english: He said to him: She is not divorced,
as we learn from Rav and Shmuel.
For Rav and Shmuel both say,
"And that is only when they are piled up and lying
in the public domain,"
and the sides of the public domain
are considered like the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת, מִדְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is not divorced. Things lying in רשות הרבים are not acquired (as רב ושמואל hold), and צידי רשות הרבים counts as רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The opposite view: she is divorced, based on רב נחמן's cow case
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא argues the reverse. רב נחמן rules that a cow pulled now, to be acquired after thirty days, is acquired even if it stands in an אגם by then. Perhaps the sides of the public street are just like that meadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, she is divorced, as we learn from רב נחמן. רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: If someone tells his friend, "Pull this cow, but it will not be acquired by you until after thirty days," the friend acquires it, even if the cow is standing in a meadow. Isn't a meadow the same as the sides of the public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא challenges רב חסדא's answer. He brings a case about acquiring a cow that seems to show she is divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב נחמן's case, the buyer acquired the cow by pulling it (משיכה) right away, and the acquisition was set to take effect after thirty days. It works even if the cow is out in an open meadow when the thirty days end, because the acquisition began properly. Here too, the woman received the גט properly at the start. So if a meadow is like צידי רשות הרבים, the delayed divorce should also work.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Pull. Acquiring an animal by pulling it (מְשִׁיכָה).
He has acquired it
A meadow or marshy open field, not owned by the buyer
Isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested proof)
This is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: The cow is in the meadow at the end of the thirty days, when the acquisition takes effect. The buyer still pulled it properly at the start.

phrases.english: On the contrary, she is divorced,
as we learn from Rav Naḥman.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: For Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
One who says to his friend:
"Pull this cow,
but it will not be acquired by you

he has acquired it,

phrases.notes: He means the cow is in the meadow when the thirty days end, not in the buyer's own property.

phrases.english: Is it not that a meadow is the same
as the sides of the public domain?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת, מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer by bringing a source that points the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that she is not divorced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A delayed acquisition that began properly still works even if the item is in an אגם when it takes effect. If an אגם is the same as צידי רשות הרבים, the delayed גט should also work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה, about pulling a cow to acquire it after thirty days.

steps.title: A meadow is not the same as the sides of the public street
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: an אגם and צידי רשות הרבים are separate kinds of places.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A meadow is one thing, and the sides of the public domain are another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects רמי בר חמא's comparison between the cow in the meadow and the גט at the side of the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule only covers an אגם. צידי רשות הרבים is a different kind of place, since רב חסדא already said it counts as the public street itself. So the cow case does not prove that she is divorced, and רב חסדא's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate, a category of its own
No (rejecting the suggested proof)

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: a delayed גט lying at צידי רשות הרבים when the time comes does not divorce her, because that place counts as רשות הרבים. רב נחמן's cow-in-the-meadow case does not prove otherwise, since an אגם is a different kind of place.

phrases.english: No, a meadow is one thing,
and the sides of the public domain are another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אֲגַם לְחוּד וְצִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison between an אגם and צידי רשות הרבים. רב נחמן's own ruling about the cow is not questioned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge treated two different kinds of place as the same.

steps.title: Second version: רב חסדא says she is divorced
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב חסדא answers רמי בר חמא's question the other way: she is divorced. This follows רב נחמן, because the sides of the public street are like an אגם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: he said to him: She is divorced, based on רב נחמן's ruling. The sides of the public street are treated like a meadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same argument. In this version רב חסדא rules that the woman is divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version רב חסדא used רב ושמואל to say 'not divorced.' Here he uses רב נחמן's cow case to say 'divorced,' treating צידי רשות הרבים like an אגם. The sides of the road are seen as a place where acquiring still works.

keyTerms.meaning: A meadow or marshy field, used in רב נחמן's cow case
The edges or sides of the public street

phrases.english: Some say: he said to him:
phrases.notes: In this version it is רב חסדא answering רמי בר חמא's question from step 2.

phrases.english: She is divorced, based on Rav Naḥman's ruling.
phrases.notes: This is the cow case from step 4: pulled now, acquired after thirty days, even if it is standing in an אגם by then.

phrases.english: And the sides of the public domain are like a meadow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת, מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the debate from steps 2-5 in a second version where the two sides are swapped.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is divorced, because צידי רשות הרבים are like an אגם, following רב נחמן.

steps.title: Challenge from רב ושמואל: she should not be divorced
steps.stepSummary: The other side argues the reverse: based on רב ושמואל she is not divorced, since the sides of the public street may be the same as the public street itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: she is not divorced, based on רב ושמואל. Isn't the rule for the public street also the rule for the sides of the public street?
steps.whatsHappening: The other side pushes back against step 6. He says the woman should NOT be divorced, based on רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל said that things lying in רשות הרבים are not acquired. The challenge assumes the sides of the street are treated just like the street. If so, the גט at the side of the street was never acquired by her.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary: the reverse is true
Is it not so that...? It opens a suggested proof
The public street or public domain

phrases.english: On the contrary: she is not divorced,
phrases.notes: In this version רמי בר חמא is the one arguing back.

phrases.english: based on Rav and Shmuel.
Is it not that this is the public domain,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: אֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת, מִדְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 6 using רב ושמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she is divorced because צידי רשות הרבים are like an אגם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If צידי רשות הרבים count as רשות הרבים, then רב ושמואל's rule applies, and nothing is acquired there.

steps.title: The public street and its sides are separate
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected: the public street and the sides of the public street are different kinds of places.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The public street is one thing, and the sides of the public street are another.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge from רב ושמואל is pushed away. רב ושמואל spoke only about the street itself, not its sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 5 with the sides swapped. There, an אגם and the sides of the street were separate. Here, the street and its sides are separate, so רב נחמן's view stands in this version.

keyTerms.meaning: Separately: a category of its own

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, each side is answered the same way: a proof from one kind of place does not carry over to a different kind of place. רשות הרבים, צידי רשות הרבים, and אגם are each their own category.

phrases.english: No, the public domain is separate,
and the sides of the public domain are separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לְחוֹד, וְצִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לְחוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between רשות הרבים and צידי רשות הרבים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ושמואל's rule was about the street itself; the sides are a different kind of place.

steps.title: New משנה: a husband may make his business-running wife swear
steps.stepSummary: A husband who makes his wife a storekeeper or a manager of his property may have her take an oath whenever he wants. רבי אליעזר says this covers even her spinning and her dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man sets up his wife as a storekeeper, or appoints her as a manager over his property, he may make her swear whenever he wants. רבי אליעזר says: even about her spinning and her dough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic. A wife who handles her husband's business can be made to swear that she took nothing that is his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows the oath because she handled his money. רבי אליעזר goes further and includes household work like spinning and baking, which has nothing to do with the store.

keyTerms.meaning: A storekeeper (woman)
A manager or steward over property
He makes her take an oath
Her spindle: the yarn she spins
Her dough

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who sets up his wife as a storekeeper,
or who appointed her as a steward,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מַשְׁבִּיעָהּ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה.
phrases.english: he may make her swear whenever he wants.
phrases.notes: The oath is that she did not take any of his things for herself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even about her spindle and about her dough.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹשִׁיב אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ חֶנְווֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the גט discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband may make his wife who runs his store or property swear at any time; רבי אליעזר extends this even to her spinning and dough.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר mean only by adding on, or from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר allows an oath about spinning and dough only by attaching it to the store oath (גלגול), or even on its own from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: Does רבי אליעזר mean through גלגול, or does he mean from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי אליעזר meant in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: once she must already swear about the store, he may add the household items onto that oath. Option two: he may make her swear about household items even when there is no store oath at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Rolling on: adding more matters onto an oath she already must take
From the start: on its own

steps.confusionAlert: גלגול does not mean a new, separate oath. It means attaching more topics onto an oath she already has to take for another reason.

phrases.english: Gemara: A question was asked of them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר עַל יְדֵי גִלְגּוּל קָאָמַר —
phrases.english: Is Rabbi Eliezer speaking about it by way of extension,
or is he speaking about it from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand רבי אליעזר's words in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר allows the household oath only through גלגול or even לכתחילה.

steps.title: Proof from the חכמים: no one lives with a snake in a basket
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים told רבי אליעזר that no one can live with a snake in a basket. That complaint makes sense if he allows the oath from the start. If it is only through גלגול, she loses nothing extra, so why complain?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: They said to רבי אליעזר: A person does not live with a snake in a basket. If you say he means from the start, that fits well. But if you say through גלגול, what difference does it make to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question from step 10. It argues that רבי אליעזר must mean from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים complained that a wife cannot live with a husband who keeps suspecting her. That complaint is strong only if he can make her swear about household items on their own. If she already must swear about the store, adding a few more items costs her nothing extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A basket
It makes sense if...
What difference does it make?

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Come and hear: They said to Rabbi Eliezer:

steps.title: She may complain about his strictness alone
steps.stepSummary: The proof from 'snake in a basket' is rejected. Even if the spinning oath only comes through גלגול, she can say his strictness makes living together impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: She might be saying to him: since you are this strict with me, I cannot live with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 11. The חכמים' complaint could make sense even if רבי אליעזר only allows the oath through גלגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 argued that if it were only גלגול, she would lose nothing new, so there would be nothing to complain about. The answer is that the hurt is in the attitude itself. A husband who checks every little thing makes the marriage unbearable, even if she takes no extra oath.

keyTerms.meaning: you are exacting, being picky and strict

live with you

steps.title: A ברייתא: the store or manager case lets him make her swear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. The first opinion says a husband who did not exempt his wife may make her swear only if he made her a storekeeper or manager.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: if a man did not free his wife from vows and oaths, and he made her a storekeeper or manager, he can make her swear whenever he wants. If he did not make her a storekeeper or manager, he cannot make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new proof by quoting a ברייתא. This first part is setup; the real proof comes from רבי אליעזר's words next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא ties the oath to a real job: running a store or managing property. Without that job, there is nothing to make her swear about. This sets up the contrast with רבי אליעזר.

vow and oath
a woman storekeeper

or appointed her as a manager —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מַשְׁבִּיעָהּ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה.
phrases.english: he may make her swear whenever he wants.
If he did not set her up as a storekeeper,
and did not appoint her as a manager —
he cannot make her swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought for the question of step 10
steps.raayaObject: The question of step 10: does רבי אליעזר allow the oath from the start?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא; this opening part gives the first opinion as background

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: every wife is a manager of her spinning and dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says even without a store or manager job, the husband can make her swear, since every wife manages her spinning and dough. This shows he allows the oath from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: even if he did not make her a storekeeper or manager, he can make her swear whenever he wants. There is no wife who was not a manager at some point in her husband's life, over her spinning and her dough. They said to him: no one can live with a snake in a basket. Learn from this: from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof itself. רבי אליעזר allows the oath even when there is no store at all, so it cannot be through גלגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גלגול needs a main oath to attach to, like a store oath. Here there is no store, and the spinning and dough are themselves the reason to swear. So רבי אליעזר must allow an oath about them from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: her spindle, her spinning work
her dough
a snake in a basket; a living situation that cannot be borne
from the start, on its own

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the משנה in step 9. There, רבי אליעזר's words came after a store case, so they could be read as גלגול. Here in the ברייתא he speaks of a case with no store at all, which is why it proves the oath is from the start.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הוֹשִׁיבָהּ חֶנְווֹנִית,
phrases.english: Even though he did not set her up as a storekeeper,
and did not appoint her as a manager,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מַשְׁבִּיעָהּ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה,
phrases.english: he may make her swear whenever he wants,
for you have no wife
who did not become a manager
for at least one hour in her husband's lifetime
over her spindle and over her dough.
They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, answering רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה.
phrases.english: A person does not live with a snake in a basket.
Learn from this: even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הוֹשִׁיבָהּ חֶנְווֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 13 and draws the proof from it
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר allows an oath about spinning and dough from the start
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's words in the ברייתא: he allows the oath even with no store, giving spinning and dough as the reason

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: רבי אליעזר allows the oath about spinning and dough from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from step 10 by accepting the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives no room for גלגול, because there is no store oath to attach to. So the answer is final: according to רבי אליעזר, the oath can come from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it; the גמרא agrees with the proof
adding an oath onto another oath that is already required

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, every wife counts as a manager of her spinning and dough. So her husband can make her swear about them from the start, not only through גלגול. The חכמים reject this as unbearable, like living with a snake in a basket.

phrases.english: Conclude from it — yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר allows an oath about spinning and dough from the start, even without גלגול.

steps.title: A husband who wrote 'I have no vow or oath on you'
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if the husband wrote that he gives up his right to make her swear, he cannot make her swear. But he can still make her heirs and those who act for her swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: if he wrote to her, "I have no vow or oath upon you," he cannot make her swear. But he can make her heirs swear, and those who come with her authority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a husband's written release protects only his wife herself, not others who claim in her place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The release was written to her personally, so it covers only her. Her heirs, or people acting for her or who bought her כתובה, are not covered. They can still be made to swear when they collect.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
he wrote to her, in the כתובה
her heirs
those who come with her authority, such as people acting for her or who bought her כתובה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion: how far the husband's release reaches. It covers the wife herself, but not people who take her place.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he wrote to her
"I have no vow or oath upon you" —
he cannot make her swear,
but he can make her heirs swear,
and those who come with her authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לָהּ נֶדֶר וּשְׁבוּעָה אֵין לִי עָלַיִךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רבי אליעזר ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A written release from oaths protects the wife herself, but not her heirs or those who come with her authority.

steps.title: Freeing her side from an oath, but only for himself
steps.stepSummary: If the husband wrote that he has no vow or oath on her, her heirs, or those who act for her, he cannot make any of them swear. His heirs still can.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote: 'I have no vow or oath upon you, your heirs, or those who come on your authority,' he cannot make her swear. Not her, not her heirs, and not those who come on her authority. But his heirs can make her, her heirs, and those who come on her authority swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second way the husband can word his release: he frees her whole side, but he speaks only for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The release covers everyone on her side: herself, her יורשים, and her agents. But he only said 'I have no oath', so the release only stops him. His own יורשים never gave up their right, so they can still make her side swear.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow and an oath: the ways a husband could make his wife swear she was honest with his property
To make someone take an oath
Heirs
Those who come on her authority: people who step into her rights, like someone she sold her כתובה to

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a release works exactly as far as its wording goes, on both sides: who is freed, and who is giving up the right.

phrases.english: "I have no vow or oath upon you
phrases.notes: These are the words the husband wrote in her כתובה.

phrases.english: or upon your heirs, or upon those who come on your authority"
he cannot make her swear,
not her, and not her heirs,
and not those who come on her authority.
But his heirs can make her swear,
and her heirs, and those who come on her authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶדֶר וּשְׁבוּעָה אֵין לִי עָלַיִךְ וְעַל יוֹרְשַׁיִךְ וְעַל הַבָּאִים בְּרִשּׁוּתֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes on from the first release wording in step 16 to a wider wording that frees her whole side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A release written only in the husband's own name frees her, her heirs, and her agents from him, but not from his heirs.

steps.title: A full release that covers both sides
steps.stepSummary: If he wrote that neither he, his heirs, nor those who act for him have any oath on her, her heirs, or those who act for her, then nobody on his side can make anyone on her side swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote: 'Neither I, nor my heirs, nor those who come on my authority have any vow or oath upon you, your heirs, or those who come on your authority,' then no one can make them swear. Not he, not his heirs, and not those who come on his authority. And they cannot make her swear, or her heirs, or those who come on her authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the widest wording: the release covers everyone on his side and everyone on her side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time he also gave up the right for his יורשים and agents. So the opening that was left in step 17, where his heirs could still demand a שבועה, is now closed. No one on his side can make anyone on her side swear.

keyTerms.meaning: My heirs: the husband speaking about his own heirs
Those who come on his authority: people who step into the husband's rights

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of release: (1) only her: he himself can still make her heirs and those who come on her authority swear; (2) her whole side, but only in his own name: his heirs can still demand an oath; (3) both sides: no one can demand an oath.

phrases.english: "I have no vow or oath,
nor do my heirs, nor those who come on my authority,

phrases.aramaic: עָלַיִךְ, וְעַל יוֹרְשַׁיִךְ, וְעַל הַבָּאִים בִּרְשׁוּתִיךְ״
phrases.english: upon you, or upon your heirs, or upon those who come on your authority"
no one can make her swear,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הוּא וְלֹא יוֹרְשָׁיו וְלֹא הַבָּאִים בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ,
phrases.english: not he, not his heirs, and not those who come on his authority,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אוֹתָהּ וְלֹא יוֹרְשֶׁיהָ, וְלֹא הַבָּאִים בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ.
phrases.english: not her, not her heirs, and not those who come on her authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶדֶר וּשְׁבוּעָה אֵין לִי, וְלֹא לְיוֹרְשַׁי, וְלֹא לַבָּאִים בִּרְשׁוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens step 17's wording by also including the husband's heirs and agents, which closes the gap left there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A release written for both sides stops everyone on his side from making anyone on her side swear.

steps.title: When the heirs can make a widow swear
steps.stepSummary: If the widow never managed the estate, the heirs cannot make her swear. If she did manage it, they can make her swear about what she did after his death, but not about the time before.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house, or went back to her father-in-law's house but did not become a manager of the property, the heirs cannot make her swear. If she did become a manager, the heirs can make her swear about what happens from now on, but not about what happened before.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now looks at a widow whose husband had freed her from an oath, and asks when his יורשים can still make her swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His release covers the time of his life, so the heirs cannot ask about that time. If she never handled the estate after he died, there is nothing new to swear about. But if she became an אפוטרופיא after his death, that new management is not covered by his release, so the heirs can make her swear about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A female manager of property
Her father-in-law's house, meaning the husband's family home
What comes in the future: here, the time after the husband's death
What already passed: here, the time while the husband was alive

steps.confusionAlert: 'Future' and 'past' are measured from the husband's death. The past is his lifetime, which his release covers. The future is her managing the estate after he died.

phrases.english: If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house,
or she went back to her father-in-law's house
and did not become a manager of the property,
the heirs cannot make her swear.
And if she became a manager,

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹרְשִׁין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא,
phrases.english: the heirs can make her swear about what is still to come,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר.
phrases.english: but they cannot make her swear about what already passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלְכָה מִקֶּבֶר בַּעְלָהּ לְבֵית אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the release from the earlier cases to work out what the heirs can ask after the husband dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A released widow can be made to swear by the heirs only about her management after the husband's death, and only if she actually managed the estate.

steps.title: What oath was there to release her from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what oath the husband could have made his wife take, that he needed to write a release from it. It begins bringing רב's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the oath for? רב יהודה said that רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion by asking what oath the משנה's release is about. It then starts bringing רב's answer, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes the husband had some שבועה he could make his wife take, but it never says what it was. The גמרא wants to know what that oath was, so we understand what the release actually gives up. The line 'רב יהודה said that רב said' only names who will answer; the answer itself comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is its purpose? What is it doing here?
רב יהודה reporting a teaching he heard from his teacher רב

phrases.english: גמרא:
The oath, what is it for?
phrases.notes: He means: what oath could he make her take while he was alive, that he had to write a release from it?

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבוּעָה מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא, asking about the oath that steps 16 to 18 assumed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What oath could the husband make his wife take, that he needed to release her from it in the כתובה?
